sentences.text: Sri K.R. Singh, learned counsel appearing for GDA, submits that the subject land was acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
An award was declared on 29.07.2010.
It is open to the petitioner to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer and pray for release of compensation.

He submits that the petitioner instead of making prayer for payment of compensation to him moved application on 29.11.2018 challenging the action of the respondents in acquiring the land and also prayed for release of the acquired land.
He submits that the case set up by the petitioner is inconsistent.
He further submits that a supplementary award was also made but that was not in relation to the subject land.

4. We have gone through the representation dated 29.11.2018 and we find the submission of Sri K.R.
Singh, learned counsel for GDA, to be correct.
The petitioner therein has prayed for release of his land.
In the subsequent representation, he has disputed the quantum of compensation awarded and has claimed a higher compensation.

5. It is also pertinent to note that in the present petition the petitioner is claiming compensation, as per Act No. 30 of 2013, which in the facts and circumstances, noted above, would not apply at all.
6. We, thus, find no merit in the petition.

It is left open to the petitioner to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer for release of compensation amount and in which event the Special Land Acquisition Officer shall consider the entitlement of the petitioner and order accordingly.
7. The petition stands disposed of.
(Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 7.2.2025 gp  Kamaluddin vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 7 February, 2025
